task: 0x27/0xa7 low-nibble-7 convert/shift + 0x07 barrier variants (0x54 residual root owner) — EXP-M4-13 R5 (n7_barrier)
kind: length-rule-edit + descriptor-add (additive; clean-room OWN-MSL / own-compiled-corpus byte-diff)
summary: Root-caused the 0x54 residual desync to a MISSING descriptor for the a7-17 int/uint->float/half convert sibling (length 8 was already correct), plus two unlengthed 0x07 low-nibble-7 ops (copysign 07 c2 88, subgroup-vote fence 07 22 22) and one unlengthed-descriptor mesh 0x27 bitfield (27 00 66). Closing these cleared 30 corpus files (17 own + 13 tp) with ZERO regression. The a7-17 root alone accounts for 14 own + 13 tp of the 0x54 residual (the bulk of the '~20 own / 30 tp' the task cited); the residual 0x54-containing leftovers that REMAIN are cascades of unrelated families (0x0b compact-move, 0x17 unpack, 0x02 icmp, 0x09 op-select) and are out of scope.

lengthRuleEdits.location: isadb.py instr_length(), the `if b0 == 0x07 and buf[off+2] in (...)` scoreboard-fence branch
lengthRuleEdits.rationale: Two 0x07 low-nibble-7 ops had NO length rule (byte+2 not in the old set) and desynced their operand tails as spurious 0x54: (a) the SUBGROUP-VOTE fence `07 22 22 80` (byte+2==0x22) — the multi-vote sibling of the already-handled single-vote `07 00 20 80` (byte+2==0x20); (b) the copysign SIGN-COMBINE op `07 c2 88 00` (byte+2==0x88). Both are 4 bytes (own-MSL confirmed for copysign; backward-tokenization-forced for both). byte+2==0x54 is still handled earlier (barrier/mem_fence/link_save, 6/8B) so this gate is never reached for it. Both new byte+2 values have bit0==0, so the existing scoreboard_fence descriptor already matched them once lengthed; copysign additionally gets a dedicated more-specific descriptor.
lengthRuleEdits.provenance: OWN-MSL: `copysign(a,b)` (float) compiles to `07 c2 88 00` byte-exact (reproduced vs committed float_arith/copysign corpus); `07 22 22 80` byte-diffed against the sibling `07 00 20 80` our own simd_all/simd_any/simd_ballot kernels emit. NOT HW-dispatch-validated.

noLengthEditNeeded.note: Length 8 was ALREADY returned by the existing `a7 byte+1 in {0x07,0x17} -> 8` rule; the ONLY gap was the missing descriptor. Descriptor-only fix (cvt_i2f_src).

Length 12 was ALREADY returned by the existing `0x27 byte+1 in {0x00,0x02,0x10} -> 12` rule; the existing ibfins descriptor required byte+2 in {0x54,0x56} and so did not match byte+2==0x66. Descriptor-only fix (ibfe_mesh_attr).

descriptors.semantics: d = float(a) ; integer/uint -> float/half convert (round to nearest even). The byte+1==0x17 sibling of cvt_i2f (byte+1==0x07): byte+1 bit4 marks the SOURCE-CONSUMED-BY-A-FOLLOWING-ALU-OP routing (byte+2==0x54 result-consumed vs 0x56 standalone/last-use); the convert itself and the byte+6 width / byte+7 sign (bit6=signed i2f vs unsigned u2f) fields are IDENTICAL to the HW-VALIDATED cvt_i2f.
descriptors.provenance: inferred (OWN-MSL byte-diff, EXP-M4-13 R5): reproduced by our own compilation of `o=float(int)+float(int)` / `float(uint)+float(uint)` and the committed conversions_pack/cvt_i2f.metal (`a7 17 54 08 03 00 8e 20`, byte-exact). The a7-07 and a7-17 forms appear TOGETHER when two converts feed one ALU combine (byte-diff: differ only in byte+1 0x07->0x17, byte+2 0x56->0x54, source descriptor; byte+6 width and byte+7 sign identical). Signed/unsigned byte+7 0x60/0x20 CONFIRMED own-MSL; the byte+1 bit4 source-routing role is byte-diff-inferred, NOT HW-splice-isolated. Same convert semantics as HW-VALIDATED cvt_i2f.

descriptors.semantics: d = copysign(a, b) = |a| with the sign bit of b (float). 4 bytes: 07 c2 88 <ops>. byte0 0x07 low-nibble-7 sign-combine ALU op; byte+3 carries the src/dst register operand descriptor. The half (fp16) copysign is a separate byte0-0x0f op, not this one.
descriptors.provenance: inferred (OWN-MSL byte-diff, EXP-M4-13 R5): our own compilation of `copysign(a[i],b[i])` (float) emits `07 c2 88 00` byte-exact vs the committed float_arith/copysign corpus (the half form is a distinct `0f c2 8a 02`). Length 4 is forced by clean whole-kernel tokenization (op followed directly by the 14B device store then the stop). byte+3 operand-descriptor role byte-diff-inferred, NOT HW-splice-isolated. More specific than scoreboard_fence (24 vs 9 match bits) so decode_one prefers it.
descriptors.note: This descriptor is MORE SPECIFIC than the existing scoreboard_fence (which also matches byte0==0x07 & byte+2 bit0==0); decode_one's max-match-bits tie-break picks copysign for `07 c2 88 xx`. Semantically it is ALU, not a memory fence.

descriptors.semantics: d = extract_bits(packed_attr, off, cnt) -- bitfield-extract of a packed flat PER-PRIMITIVE mesh attribute in the fragment stage (source-address mode byte+2==0x66). 12-byte operand form (byte+8==0xf0 register-operand tail), the same bitfield-extract family as the 0xa7 ibfe / 0x27 ibfins but with the mesh packed-attribute source mode.
descriptors.provenance: inferred (byte-diff, EXP-M4-13 R5): single occurrence in our OWN-MSL mesh_pervertex_wide fragment (`27 00 66 00 03 14 42 00 f0 10 01 00`), unpacking the flat `uint pid [[flat]]` per-primitive attribute (`float(in.p.pid)*0.01`). Length 12 gives clean tokenization of the mesh-fragment prologue; field roles byte-diff-inferred, NOT HW-splice-isolated. Single own-corpus occurrence, 0 in thirdparty.

reuses: scoreboard_fence — the subgroup-vote fence `07 22 22 80` (byte+2==0x22) now decodes through the EXISTING scoreboard_fence descriptor once the length gate above admits byte+2==0x22 (byte+2 bit0==0 already matched). No new descriptor for the 0x22 form; only the length edit. scoreboard_fence's semantics text could optionally note the byte+2==0x22 subgroup-vote form.
notes: The task hypothesis ('0x54 residual are operand tails of a mis-lengthed 0x27/0xa7') is HALF-confirmed: the dominant root (a7-17, 14 own + 13 tp) was NOT a mis-length but a MISSING DESCRIPTOR at an already-correct length 8 — the length-8 read had no matching descriptor, so decode_one raised at a clean boundary and exposed the 8-byte tail (which contains byte+2==0x54). Adding the descriptor closes it. No 0xa7/0x27 op in the corpus was found to be genuinely mis-LENGTHED (a7 20->12, a7 00->12, 27 10->12 etc. were all verified correct by backward tokenization).
The two 0x07 ops (copysign, subgroup-vote) WERE genuinely unlengthed (length_unknown) — a true length-rule gap, now closed.
